textbookBox.ref: CBSE Class 6 social-science · Landforms and Life · Textbook Concepts
textbookBox.concept: A landform is a physical feature on the surface of the Earth. Landforms take shape over millions of years and are closely linked with the environment and life.

1.tip: Look closely at the diagram on the board as we explain each property.

beats.en: A landform is a physical feature on the surface of the Earth. Landforms take shape over millions of years and are closely linked with the environment and life.
beats.speakEn: A landform is a physical feature on the surface of the Earth. Landforms take shape over millions of years and are closely linked with the environment and life.

beats.en: Mountains are landforms much higher than the land around them. You can recognise a mountain by its broad base, steep slopes and narrow summit. Height above sea level is called altitude.
beats.speakEn: Mountains are landforms much higher than the land around them. You can recognise a mountain by its broad base, steep slopes and narrow summit. Height above sea level is called altitude.

type: Key Concept: A landform is a physical feature on the surface of the Earth.
Rule: Mountains are landforms much higher than the land around them.

textbookBox.ref: CBSE Class 6 social-science · Landforms and Life · Deeper Textbook Ideas
textbookBox.concept: Mountain terrain is rough with steep slopes, so regular farming is possible only in some valleys. Farmers cut steps into the slope and grow crops on them, which is called terrace farming.

beats.en: Mountain terrain is rough with steep slopes, so regular farming is possible only in some valleys. Farmers cut steps into the slope and grow crops on them, which is called terrace farming.
beats.speakEn: Mountain terrain is rough with steep slopes, so regular farming is possible only in some valleys. Farmers cut steps into the slope and grow crops on them, which is called terrace farming.

beats.en: A plateau rises above the land around it and has a more or less flat top, with some steep sides. Plateaus can be young or old, and their height varies from a few hundred metres to several thousand.
beats.speakEn: A plateau rises above the land around it and has a more or less flat top, with some steep sides. Plateaus can be young or old, and their height varies from a few hundred metres to several thousand.

type: Mountain terrain is rough with steep slopes, so regular farming is possible only in some valleys.

textbookBox.ref: CBSE Class 6 social-science · Landforms and Life · Complete Summary
textbookBox.concept: Plains are landforms with an extensive flat or gently rolling surface and no large hills or deep valleys. They are generally not more than 300 metres above sea level.

beats.en: Let us review the key takeaway from Landforms and Life: Plains are landforms with an extensive flat or gently rolling surface and no large hills or deep valleys. They are generally not more than 300 metres above sea level.
